Article Title: UP Creators Summit & Awards to celebrate the state's rising digital voices and creator economy in grand 2-day event
Article Text:
Times of India’s UP Creators Summit & Awards

Honouring the creators shaping a new Uttar Pradesh

Conversations driving the future of the creator economy

Preparing creators for the future

As India's creator economy continues to redefine entertainment, entrepreneurship and storytelling, Uttar Pradesh is emerging as one of the country's fastest-growing hubs for digital innovation. With increasing internet penetration, a thriving startup ecosystem and the rapid rise of creators from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, the state is playing a pivotal role in shaping India's digital future.Celebrating this transformation, the inaugural edition Times of India’s UP Creators Summit & Awards will bring together some of the state's most influential content creators, industry leaders, brands and digital innovators for a 2-day mega showcase of recognition, insightful conversations and future-focused learning.To be held on August 19 and 20 in Varanasi, the spiritual and cultural heart of Uttar Pradesh, the event will bring together the state’s rich heritage and its new-age digital voices, showcasing how creators are shaping the narrative of a new Uttar Pradesh. The first day, August 19, will feature insightful masterclasses, panel discussions and fireside chats, while August 20 will culminate in the grand UP Creators Awards, celebrating the state’s most impactful digital creators.At the heart of the event are the Creators Awards, which will honour creators who are making a meaningful impact across diverse genres, including education, technology, finance, food, travel, lifestyle, comedy, fashion, gaming, social impact and more. These creators are not only building communities online but are also amplifying local stories, inspiring millions and showcasing Uttar Pradesh's talent on the national and global stage. The awards celebrate creators who are redefining digital influence while contributing to the state's growing reputation as a powerhouse of innovation and creativity.Beyond the awards, the summit will serve as a platform for thought-provoking discussions on the opportunities and challenges shaping the creator ecosystem.Panel discussions will explore how the creator economy is expanding beyond metropolitan cities into Tier 2 and Tier 3 India, the growing influence of creators in rebranding Uttar Pradesh, and the role of digital storytellers in building the narrative of a new Uttar Pradesh. The event will also feature engaging fireside chats on themes such as "Storytellers of a New Bharat" and "Beyond Followers", examining how creators are moving beyond metrics to create meaningful impact, influence culture and build sustainable careers.As artificial intelligence reshapes the content landscape, the summit will host a dedicated AI Masterclass on future-proofing content creation. The session will provide practical insights into how creators can leverage AI-powered tools to enhance creativity, improve productivity and stay ahead in an increasingly competitive digital ecosystem.Bringing together creators, policymakers, industry experts and ecosystem enablers, the UP Creators Summit & Awards aims to celebrate the diverse voices driving India's digital revolution while highlighting Uttar Pradesh's emergence as one of the country's most exciting creator hubs. More than just an awards platform, the summit will spotlight the ideas, conversations and collaborations that are shaping the future of content creation in India.
Article Summary: Times of india’s up creators summit & awards will be held on august 19 and 20 in varanasi, the spiritual and cultural heart of uttar pradesh. The event will honour creators who are making a meaningful impact across diverse genres, including education, technology, finance, food, travel, lifestyle, comedy, fashion, gaming, social impact and more.

Article Title: AI, jobs, free coaching & sports: What PM Modi offered Gen Z on Independence Day
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi interacts with students during the 80th Independence Day celebrations, at Red Fort in New Delhi. (PTI Photo)

AI training for 1 crore youth

Free online coaching for competitive exams

Sports talent hunt for children aged 5 to 15

Jobs, manufacturing and MSMEs

Start-up and technology opportunities

Defence, green economy and creative industries

From ‘Fragile Five’ to a growing economy

NEW DELHI: From artificial intelligence training for one crore young people to free online coaching for competitive examinations, Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Independence Day speech had several announcements aimed directly at India's youth, with technology, jobs, entrepreneurship and skills forming a key part of the message.Addressing the nation from the Red Fort on the 80th Independence Day, PM Modi said India's youth would be the biggest beneficiary as well as the biggest enabler of the country's ambition to become a developed nation by 2047. He linked the Viksit Bharat goal to the country's young population and outlined initiatives spanning AI, education, sports, manufacturing and entrepreneurship.PM Modi announced that one crore youth would be trained in artificial intelligence-related skills. The announcement came as he described AI, quantum technology, robotics, space and data centres as defining technologies of the current era and called for India to become a global hub of innovation."When I speak of a developed India, when I speak of propelling the nation forward at a rapid pace, the greatest beneficiary and the greatest enabler of this vision is the youth of my country, the youthful energy of my nation.Not only that, but the greatest beneficiary of a developed India is also the youth of my country. Therefore, we must advance the goal of a developed India by linking it with our youth," PM Modi said.For students and young people preparing for government and other competitive examinations, PM Modi announced free online coaching. The initiative was among the youth-focused measures announced during the address.The prime minister also announced a nationwide sports talent hunt to identify and nurture children aged five to 15 years across villages and cities, expanding the focus on identifying sporting talent at an early age.AI was one of the biggest technology-related announcements in PM Modi's speech. He said one crore young people would receive training in AI skills as India seeks to build capabilities in emerging technologies.PM Modi placed the initiative within his broader 'Shakti Ki Saptadhara' framework, under which technology and innovation form the third stream of India's development strategy."The third strength of the Saptadhara is technology and innovation. This is the era of robotics, AI, quantum technology, space and data centres. Emerging technologies are presenting new challenges, and we must become a global hub of innovation," PM Modi said.He also pointed to India's existing digital infrastructure, including UPI and Digital Public Infrastructure, and said the country needed to take the next step in emerging technologies."We have already demonstrated our strength through UPI and Digital Public Infrastructure. Now, we must take the next leap in next-generation communication technology," he added.The AI training plan comes as PM Modi has repeatedly linked India's young workforce with the country's technology ambitions, with the latest announcement putting a specific focus on building AI-related skills at scale.For young people preparing for competitive examinations, PM Modi announced free online coaching.The initiative is aimed at making preparation resources available to youth without requiring them to rely exclusively on physical coaching centres.PM Modi said, "The race for coaching classes has become a massive burden for our middle-class families. Every parent feels that if they don't send their child to a coaching class, they aren't considered a 'prestigious' family. We are concerned about the thousands of crores of rupees these poor and middle-class families spend; we want to save them that expense. We have decided to provide free online coaching for various competitive exams for our youth. We have digital public infrastructure, as well as excellent talent and teachers. By leveraging these resources, we are establishing a comprehensive network to provide free coaching to the nation's youth."The announcement was made alongside the AI skilling plan as part of the government's broader focus on connecting India's youth with opportunities created by the country's development and technology push.PM Modi said the country's development target must be linked directly with young people, describing them as both the principal beneficiaries and enablers of Viksit Bharat.PM Modi also announced a nationwide sports talent hunt to identify and nurture children between five and 15 years of age.The programme will cover children in villages as well as cities, with the focus on identifying sporting talent at an early age and developing it further.The announcement adds sports to the list of areas through which the government plans to connect young Indians with the broader Viksit Bharat vision.PM Modi also referred to the growing role of women in sports, STEM education, aviation and the armed forces during his address.Beyond direct youth-focused announcements, PM Modi's seven-point roadmap placed manufacturing, agriculture, technology, infrastructure, defence, green and blue economy, and soft power at the centre of India's growth strategy.For Gen Z entering the workforce, manufacturing and MSMEs were among the sectors PM Modi highlighted as areas with global opportunities.He urged Indian businesses, particularly MSMEs, to use free trade agreements to take Indian products to international markets."We have to reach the world. Everything that India produces should reach the world market," Modi said.PM Modi said Indian products in sectors such as textiles, machinery, pharmaceuticals, fisheries and seafood should expand their presence in global markets. He also stressed that companies would need to compete on international standards of cost, quality and scale.In manufacturing, PM Modi said India should become a reliable hub in global supply chains."From Design to Manufacturing, India must become a reliable hub in the global supply chain. For this, I want to place special emphasis on 3 things. My brothers and sisters in the field of Manufacturing, do not let this opportunity slip away. For this, we will have to meet global standards on cost, quality, and scale," PM Modi said.Technology and innovation were central to PM Modi's seven-point roadmap, with AI, quantum technology, robotics, space and data centres identified as areas where India should develop global capabilities."The third strength of the Saptadhara is technology and innovation. This is the era of robotics, AI, quantum technology, space and data centres. Emerging technologies are presenting new challenges, and we must become a global hub of innovation," PM Modi said.The prime minister also called for India to take the lead in next-generation communication technology, including 6G.For young entrepreneurs and technology professionals, PM Modi also spoke about the need for Indian technology companies to build globally recognised brands."India's technology companies should be a scoreboard in the world," he said.PM Modi's roadmap also identified defence production, the green economy and India's soft power as areas for future growth.In defence, he called for self-reliance and the development of next-generation defence technologies, with India aiming to become a global supplier."The importance of defence capability is paramount in every sense. My dear citizens, achieving Aatmanirbharta in defence is essential; India and the world have realised that there is no alternative. When the world looks out for itself, India cannot merely remain an arms market for other nations," he said.The sixth stream, the green and blue economy, covers renewable energy, energy storage, green manufacturing, fisheries, coastal tourism and ocean technology."The sixth strength of the Sapta Dhara is the Green economy. We must work in the areas of renewable energy, energy storage, green storage and manufacturing. India has an opportunity in the area of the Blue Economy. "The seventh stream is India's soft power, covering yoga, Ayurveda, handicrafts, culture, films, animation, gaming and digital content."The seventh strength of the Sapta Dhara is India's soft power. Today, Yoga has connected the world to India. Our Ayurveda, holistic healthcare, handicrafts, culture, films, animation, gaming, digital content. The world is recognizing and looking forward to India's WAVES summit. We have more than 100 national parks. We have an opportunity to attract foreign tourists through the power of soft power."PM Modi also used his Independence Day address to highlight India's economic transformation over the past 12 years, saying the country had moved from the 'Fragile Five' to becoming the world's fastest-growing major economy.He said India was now aiming for a larger role in global manufacturing, technology and trade and set out a goal of building Viksit Bharat by 2047.PM Modi cited growth in defence production, electronic manufacturing, railway coach production, internet use and digital transactions as indicators of the country's economic and technological expansion.He also announced that India had begun production at three semiconductor plants, with five to eight more plants expected to come up in the coming years.For Gen Z, the message running through PM Modi's youth-focused announcements was centred on acquiring skills in emerging technologies, accessing education and competitive-exam preparation, identifying sporting talent and participating in sectors that the government has identified as drivers of India's growth.
Article Summary: Pm modi announced that one crore youth would be trained in artificial intelligence-related skills. He also announced a nationwide sports talent hunt to identify and nurture children aged five to 15 years across villages and cities. For young people preparing for competitive examinations, pm modi announced free online coaching.

Article Title: Cockroaches, expired food: Maharashtra FDA suspends 14 licences linked to Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart
Article Text:
Inspections uncovered violations ranging from cockroach infestation and expired food to poor hygiene and storage practices.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licences of 14 food business establishments linked to quick-commerce platforms Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart after a statewide inspection drive uncovered multiple food safety and hygiene violations.The August 13 drive covered 86 establishments across Maharashtra involved in the storage, sale and delivery of food through online platforms. The FDA issued 60 improvement notices and ordered one facility to temporarily halt operations, news agency PTI reported.Of the 14 suspended licences, five were linked to Blinkit, five to Zepto, two to Instamart, while one each belonged to Bhagwati Stores and Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd.The inspections focused on storage conditions, temperature control, cleanliness, pest management, personal hygiene of food handlers, food safety records, display of licences and compliance with inventory practices such as First In, First Out (FIFO) and First Expired, First Out (FEFO).In Pune, the FDA suspended the licence of a Zepto outlet in Lohegaon after inspectors found food items stored beyond their declared "use by" dates.The regulator also flagged unhygienic storage conditions, inadequate pest control and lapses in personal hygiene, adding that the company's response during the hearing was unsatisfactory.Another Pune facility operated by Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd was found to have a cockroach infestation, inadequate cold-chain maintenance for frozen products and deficiencies in hygiene and pest-control practices.In Mumbai, a Blinkit facility in Malad (West) was found to be operating with chiller temperatures above the prescribed limit. Inspectors also found that around 40 food handlers had not undergone mandatory medical examinations and that records were unavailable.The FDA said several workers were not using protective gear such as gloves, aprons and head coverings. Inspectors also found damaged storage racks, poor organisation and inadequate segregation of different categories of food products.At another Blinkit facility in Ghatkopar, officials flagged shortcomings in drainage, waste disposal, temperature control and housekeeping. The outlet was classified as non-compliant after scoring 46 per cent during the inspection.Inspections at Zepto facilities in Mulund and Goregaon revealed deficiencies related to food storage, temperature management, cleanliness and licence display.At an Instamart outlet in Andheri, inspectors found food packets stored directly on the floor. The FDA also reported inadequate storage space, overcrowding and deficiencies in hygiene and temperature control.The inspection drive also covered delivery operations.At a Blinkit store in Karad in Satara district, officials checked 125 delivery riders and found that they lacked identity cards and medical fitness records. The regulator also found that the outlet's FSSAI licence was not displayed on delivery bags and boxes.The FDA directed the company to suspend two-wheeler delivery operations at the outlet until the deficiencies were addressed.The regulator said the action was taken under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and urged all food businesses operating through online platforms to strictly comply with prescribed food safety, hygiene and storage standards.
Article Summary: Inspections uncovered violations ranging from cockroach infestation and expired food to poor hygiene and storage practices. Maharashtra food and drug administration (fda) has suspended the licences of 14 food business establishments linked to quick-commerce platforms blinkit, zepto and instamart.

Article Title: Go chemical-free to tap global agri market, says PM Modi
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Identifying agriculture and food production as the "second strength" of the seven streams (Sapta Dhara) of power that can take India to "new heights" in the next 5-7 years, PM Narendra Modi Saturday pitched for transitioning to chemical-free farming and creating integrated farm-to-export supply chains for millets, spices and fruits."We have to move from the farm to the export market. Whether it is our traditional cuisine, our millets, our spices, our fruits or our flowers, we have so much to offer. These should become global brands. Our farmers should give greater impetus to chemical-free farming, as the demand for such products is only going to increase across the world," said Modi. He said, "If our agricultural products meet global parameters in every respect, we will be able to reach markets across the world with ease. "Absence of supply chain is currently one of the main obstacles before farmers in moving towards crop diversification. Despite attempts to move towards climate-resilient millets, farmers have not found millets as attractive as water-guzzling sugarcane and paddy in terms of getting an assured income.Govt's focus on tapping the global market through export promotion and creation of adequate supply chains may be an effective step towards crop diversification, to attain the twin goals of increasing farmers' income and promoting sustainable farming through judicious use of inputs."We must move forward in the direction of food processing as well... Because of FTAs, we are getting access to a very large market, and we must reach them. ..," said the PM while outlining the seven streams (Sapta Dhara) of power before the country. He identified "manufacturing" as the first strength and "technology and innovation" as the third strength of the seven streams that can pave the way for a developed India by 2047.
Article Summary: Pm narendra modi saturday pitched for transitioning to chemical-free farming and creating integrated farm-to-export supply chains for millets, spices and fruits. He identified agriculture and food production as the "second strength" of the seven streams that can take india to "new heights" in the next 5-7 years.

Article Title: Food regulator failed to penalise 2,430 firms: CAG
Article Text:
Food safety officials inspected 26 Bengaluru hotels on Friday. Thirty teams collected 35 food samples for laboratory analysis

NEW DELHI: The food regulator failed to impose Rs 5.60 crore in penalties on 2,430 food businesses that either did not file or delayed filing mandatory annual returns, a CAG audit has found, raising questions over enforcement of basic food safety rules.An audit of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India's (FSSAI) Eastern Region office in Kolkata found that 1,018 food businesses did not submit their annual returns, while 1,412 filed them late during 2017-18 to 2022-23.These returns provide FSSAI with information on the quantities of food products manufactured, handled, imported or exported by licensed food businesses during the year. They have to be submitted by May 31. Businesses that miss the deadline are liable to pay a penalty of Rs 100 for each day of delay, subject to the prescribed limit.CAG estimated that Rs 5.60 crore in penalties should have been imposed on the 2,430 businesses. However, the audit found that FSSAI had not imposed the penalties. It also noted that none of the defaulters had their licence suspended or cancelled as of August 2023.Following the audit, FSSAI said improvement notices had been issued to some defaulting food businesses and that notices would be issued again to all defaulters.Of the Rs 5.60 crore penalty identified by CAG, Rs 2.27 crore had been recovered, according to the report.The finding is significant because filing an annual return is a basic requirement for licensed food businesses. The audit has highlighted gaps in FSSAI's monitoring and enforcement of this requirement.
Article Summary: 1,018 food businesses did not submit their annual returns, while 1,412 filed them late. Cag estimated that rs 5.60 crore in penalties should have been imposed on the 2,430 businesses. None of the defaulters had their licence suspended or cancelled as of 2023.

Article Title: 5 indigenous small modular reactors targeted by 2033, Jitendra Singh tells LS
Article Text:
Union MoS Jitendra Singh speaks in the Lok Sabha during the Monsoon session of Parliament

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A key objective of the govt under the Nuclear Energy Mission is to develop and operationalise at least five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033, minister for department of atomic energy Jitendra Singh said in a written reply in the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is undertaking the design and development of indigenous SMR technologies, including the 220 MWe Bharat Small Modular Reactor (BSMR-200) and 55 MWe SMR-55 for power generation. BARC is also developing a high temperature gas cooled reactor (HTGCR) of up to 5 MW capacity, which can be coupled with a suitable thermochemical cycle for hydrogen production.Singh said India is steadily strengthening its indigenous nuclear energy ecosystem with a focus on advanced reactor technologies, SMRs, domestic manufacturing capabilities, private-sector participation and long-term utilisation of the country’s abundant thorium resources. The govt has adopted a two-pronged approach to accelerate nuclear capacity addition. This includes deployment of large indigenous reactors such as 700 MWe pressurised heavy water reactors (PHWRs) and advanced reactor designs at greenfield sites, alongside development and deployment of SMRs at brownfield locations, including retiring fossil-fuel-based power plants, captive plants for energy-intensive industries and off-grid applications in remote areas.The minister also highlighted continuing work of the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) in advancing the second stage of India’s nuclear power programme. IGCAR is pursuing multidisciplinary scientific research and advanced engineering development for sodium cooled fast breeder reactors and associated closed fuel-cycle facilities, technologies that remain a cornerstone of India’s long-term nuclear strategy.On thorium, Singh said India is pursuing its three-stage nuclear power programme, based on a closed fuel cycle, to optimise utilisation of its uranium resources and progressively harness its abundant thorium reserves. Thorium, being a fertile material, needs to be converted into fissile uranium-233 in a nuclear reactor before it can be used for energy generation.India has already undertaken sustained R&D towards thorium utilisation. Thorium Oxide (Thoria) pellets have been used in the initial cores of operating PHWRs, while Thoria-based fuels have also been irradiated in BARC research reactors. The irradiated Thoria pins have been reprocessed to obtain uranium-233, which has subsequently been fabricated as fuel for the KAMINI reactor at IGCAR, Kalpakkam. Singh said the Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, 2025 has been enacted to enable wider participation of both public and private entities in the nuclear sector.
Article Summary: The govt under the nuclear energy mission is to develop and operationalise at least five indigenous small modular reactors by 2033. Bhabha atomic research centre (barc) is undertaking the design and development of indigenous smr technologies. The govt has adopted a two-pronged approach to accelerate nuclear capacity addition.

Article Title: Who is Gautam Rangarajan? Indian-origin strategist appointed to key role by UK PM Andy Burnham
Article Text:
Indian-origin strategist Gautam Rangarajan.

Who is Gautam Rangarajan ?

What will Gautam Rangarajan do at No. 10?

Burnham's government overhaul

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Indian-origin strategist and former BBC executive Gautam Rangarajan as an Expert Adviser on Structure and Process in a newly created role at 10 Downing Street.Rangarajan, who brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media, is set to take up the position this week.Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive with more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting.Before his new government role, he spent more than 30 years at the BBC, beginning his career as a radio music producer and eventually rising to become the broadcaster's Group Director for Strategy and Performance.His experience includes developing strategy in rapidly changing markets, leading large-scale transformation initiatives and handling complex policy and financial negotiations.The exact details of Rangarajan's responsibilities are yet to be outlined. Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox: "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with…" - a lesson on humour, perspective and facing hard times with lightness
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox (AP photo)

Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox

"I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor"

Where this quote actually comes from

Why humour matters most during genuinely difficult stretches

How humour actually helps people manage stress

Why laughing at your own mistakes actually matters

Why humour can genuinely strengthen relationships

Michael J. Fox's own perspective on adversity

Why humour is not the same thing as avoiding a real problem

Why being naturally serious is not actually a flaw

Other memorable quotes by Michael J. Fox

"One's dignity may be assaulted, vandalized and cruelly mocked, but it can never be taken away unless it is surrendered."

"I am careful not to confuse excellence with perfection."

"Family is not an important thing. It's everything."

"Acceptance doesn't mean resignation; it means understanding that something is what it is and that there's got to be a way through it."

Why people still find meaning in this quote

Humour can genuinely change how a difficult moment actually feels. A stressful situation seems lighter once someone finds a reason to laugh, and a serious problem often becomes easier to approach once it can be seen from another angle. It can create a little distance from fear, frustration and uncertainty, even when the circumstances themselves have not changed. Michael J. Fox , the actor and Parkinson's disease advocate, put a striking twist on that idea. "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor," he said. Not being able to laugh, in his framing, is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life, and coming from someone who has lived with a serious, lifelong illness for decades, the line carries a good deal more weight than a passing joke.This line comes from an interview Fox gave to journalist Amy Wallace, published on Reader's Digest's website. Fox is not really suggesting that a humourless person is dangerous in any literal sense. He is pointing at the seriousness that tends to surround someone who cannot laugh at themselves, cannot recognise irony, and cannot find any lightness in a genuinely difficult moment. Humour creates real distance from a problem.It lets someone acknowledge that something is hard without letting it completely take over.Life inevitably brings disappointment, uncertainty and real stress. Humour cannot solve every problem on its own, but it can genuinely change how someone responds to one. Being able to laugh during a hard period offers a small emotional break, and it can help people communicate when a direct, serious conversation feels too uncomfortable to actually have. None of this means every situation deserves to be treated as a joke. Humour and genuine seriousness can exist side by side.Stress tends to narrow someone's attention down entirely onto the immediate problem in front of them. A moment of real laughter can interrupt that cycle. Research into humour and stress has suggested that positive humour can genuinely influence mood and help people cope with stressful experiences, and laughter itself is linked to physiological changes, including a release of muscle tension. None of this should be overstated. Humour is never a substitute for professional help or a practical solution when someone faces a genuinely serious problem. As an everyday coping tool, though, it can offer a genuinely useful shift in perspective.One of the most valuable forms of humour is simply being able to laugh at your own missteps. Nobody gets everything right. People mispronounce words, misjudge situations and occasionally embarrass themselves, and someone who can acknowledge a mistake without being consumed by embarrassment tends to find it easier to actually learn from it. Self-directed humour also tends to make social interactions considerably more comfortable, since it signals that a person does not expect flawless perfection from either themselves or anyone else around them.Shared laughter helps people form real connections. Friends, colleagues and family members often use humour to build a sense of familiarity and trust, and a well-placed joke can break tension that a serious conversation might struggle to shift on its own. There is an important line here worth being clear about, between humour that actually brings people together and humour that humiliates someone else. Jokes built on cruelty or prejudice tend to damage relationships rather than genuinely strengthen them, and the most constructive kind of humour has never really needed anyone else to get hurt.Fox became one of the most recognisable actors of his generation through films and television, including Back to the Future and Family Ties. In 1991, at the age of 29, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He later made the diagnosis public and became a prominent advocate for Parkinson's research through the Michael J. Fox Foundation. His public approach to living with the condition has consistently included honesty, genuine optimism and humour, which gives his comments about laughter an extra dimension. His point was never that difficult experiences are inherently funny. It is that holding onto a sense of humour can help someone preserve real perspective while actually facing a genuine challenge. His decades-long relationship with humour, cultivated alongside a chronic illness he never chose, reveals that laughter was never a denial of hardship for Fox, but a deliberate, hard-won tool for maintaining perspective and genuine hope through real adversity.There is a meaningful difference between using humour to cope with something difficult and using it to avoid actually dealing with it at all. Some problems genuinely require serious attention and real action, and nobody can simply laugh away financial difficulty, illness or grief. What humour can offer instead is a small amount of emotional breathing space while someone continues addressing the actual underlying issue, which is really the whole distinction worth holding onto here.Fox's quote is deliberately provocative, and it should not be read as suggesting that serious people are inherently unpleasant. Some people naturally have quieter personalities, or simply express humour in a different way. The broader lesson is really about flexibility rather than personality type. Someone who can be genuinely serious when it matters, while still finding moments of humour elsewhere, tends to have more ways of responding to life's challenges than someone who treats every single situation with exactly the same level of weight.Humour is easy to underrate, since it can look insignificant next to more obviously serious qualities like intelligence or discipline. Even so, the ability to laugh genuinely shapes how people communicate, handle their own mistakes and respond to real difficulty. Fox's quote offers a deliberately provocative reminder that life does not always need to be approached with complete seriousness. There will be moments when humour is genuinely inappropriate, and problems that cannot be laughed away at all. In between those moments, though, holding onto a sense of humour tends to keep people connected, flexible and hopeful, which is really the whole point behind the line.
Article Summary: "i think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor" michael j. Fox, actor and parkinson's disease advocate. Not being able to laugh is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life. Michael j. Fox was one of the most recognisable actors of his generation.

Article Title: OpenAI ‘loses’ another top executive as chief revenue officer Denise Dresser resigns: Read her Linkedin post
Article Text:
Read Denise Dresser’s full post on LinkedIn

Team,

I wanted to let you know that I made the difficult decision to leave OpenAI in the coming weeks to pursue other opportunities.

The opportunity to work hands-on with the most transformative technology in the world has been nothing short of incredible. I am so proud of what we have accomplished and, even more, of how this team has shown up for our customers and one another.

OpenAI sees high-stakes departure ahead of IPO

OpenAI chief revenue officer Denise Dresser is stepping down after less than a year with the ChatGPT-maker, adding to a wave of high-profile leadership departures as the firm prepares for an anticipated initial public offering (IPO). OpenAI said that Dresser is leaving to “pursue other opportunities.” To fill the vacancy, the company has appointed Dali Rajic, former President and Chief Operating Officer of cybersecurity firm Wiz, as its new Chief Revenue Officer, as per a report by CNBC.Dresser confirmed her resignation in a post on LinkedIn, expressing gratitude for her time leading the company's enterprise expansion.“Sharing the note I sent to the team today. I’m incredibly proud of all we’ve accomplished together and deeply grateful to the extraordinary people and customers who made this chapter so meaningful. I’m excited for what lies ahead and will be cheering this remarkable team on every step of the way,” she said in a post on LinkedIn.Dresser’s resignation arrives at a critical operational moment for OpenAI. The company confidentially filed its IPO prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June, following a funding round that valued the startup at $852 billion. Hired in December after more than a decade as an executive at Salesforce, Dresser was tasked with accelerating OpenAI's commercial revenue and competing against chief rival Anthropic for lucrative corporate contracts.Dresser is the second top executive to exit OpenAI this week, following Brad Lightcap’s announcement that he was departing the company to launch a new venture. The recent string of high-level exits includes Fidji Simo, the former product and business chief who stepped down last month due to health recovery.Brad Lightcap, who served as COO, an eight-year OpenAI veteran, announced his resignation on Tuesday. Three senior executives, including former head of the Sora video division Bill Peebles, departed the company in April.

The company has appointed dali rajic, former president and chief operating officer of cybersecurity firm wiz, as its new chief revenue officer. Dresser was hired in december after more than a decade as an executive at salesforce.

Article Title: Instagram gets first logo update in 10 years, internet jokes it now reads 'Instagzam'
Article Text:
Instagram's new logo

Instagram head Adam Mosseri says it was time for a refresh

Internet quickly pokes fun at new Instagram logo

Meta-owned photo sharing platform Instagram has rolled out its first logo update in a decade. But the redesign is already drawing mixed reactions online. While Meta says the new wordmark is "cleaner and more modern," many users have joked that the updated lettering makes the app's name difficult to read. Some said it looks like "Instagzam," while others compared it to "Instagwam" and even questioned whether the new design meets accessibility standards. The app's familiar multicoloured camera icon remains unchanged, with only the wordmark at the top of the app getting a new look.Announcing the redesign, Instagram head Adam Mosseri said the company wanted to modernise the logo after keeping it unchanged for 10 years.“The wordmark at the top of the app hasn't changed in 10 years, so it was time for a refresh,” Mosseri wrote in an Instagram post. He added, “Cleaner and more modern, with references to the original and the simplicity and craft that's always made it Instagram.”Mosseri also shared the announcement on Threads, writing, "Thought I'd share this on Threads [too] and see what the hot takes might be."The redesigned wordmark quickly became a talking point on Instagram and X (formerly Twitter), with many users saying some of the letters are difficult to recognise.One user commented, "Is it just me or It reads : instagzam ❓."Another wrote, "Instagwam – how a toddler would pronounce it. Perfect."Others joked that the logo looked like "Instaguam," while another user said, "It's barely readable. Does it even pass accessibility checks? Booo. I might be the outspoken minority, but do not like."While the logo attracted plenty of attention, some users said Instagram should focus on other issues affecting the platform. "Adam, while Instagram gets a new look, thousands of legitimate creators and businesses are losing their accounts without clear explanations or real support," said one user responding to Mosseri’s post.
Article Summary: Instagram has rolled out its first logo update in a decade. Many users have joked that the updated lettering makes the app's name difficult to read. The app's familiar multicoloured camera icon remains unchanged, with only the wordmark at the top of the app getting a new look.

Article Title: Phoebe Gates’ shopping app Phia responds to 'cookie stuffing' allegations, says have started issuing ...
Article Text:
Phoebe Gates' Phia responds to cookie stuffing allegations

What Phia spokesperson said

What is cookie stuffing that Phoebe Gates’ Phia is accused of

Phia, the AI-powered shopping startup founded by Bill Gates daughter Phoebe Gates and her Stanford roommate Sophia Kianni said that it is reviewing every transaction carefully and will reverse sales that were incorrectly attributed to it, says a report by People. The development comes days after a Bloomberg report said that the two founders were aware of ‘cookie stuffing’ – a practice where affiliate tracking cookies are placed on a user's browser without their knowledge, allowing a company to claim commission on purchases even when it did not influence the sale. The report cites internal Slack messages, people familiar with the matter and historical source code saying that both Gates and Kianni were aware of automatic cookie-setting features months earlier.The People report quotes a Phia spokesperson who told the publication:“Any features causing misattributions were immediately removed over a month ago on July 7. We are reviewing every transaction, we are fully committed to and have already begun issuing all transaction reversals to brand partners as a result of any misattribution, and we are hiring a head of compliance to make sure something like this never happens again.”“We are now continuing to connect our users with items and offers from thousands of brand partners,” the spokesperson continued, further adding “We will learn from this and want to ensure our users have the best possible shopping experience, with features like our new digital closet and more to come.”The statement did not address Bloomberg’s latest accusationsPhia operates as a browser extension designed to help shoppers automatically find discount codes and compare prices at online checkout counters. In exchange, partner retailers pay the platform an affiliate commission when its software helps convert a sale.However, internal chats accessed by the publication reveal that Phia implemented automated features that injected its tracking cookies into a shopper’s checkout session without requiring any user interaction, such as clicking a deal link or applying a coupon code, the Bloomberg report said. By dropping tracking identifiers automatically, Phia claimed credit and commissions for transactions it did not drive, a practice widely known as cookie stuffing and that is strictly prohibited by commercial network contracts and partner agreements.
Article Summary: Phoebe gates' phia responds to cookie stuffing allegations. Spokesperson: we are reviewing every transaction, we are fully committed to and have already begun issuing all transaction reversals to brand partners. Bloomberg report said that the two founders were aware of ‘cookie stuffing’

Article Title: China takes aim at Elon Musk’s ‘Jesus-level’ brain-chip dream with first BCI surgery policy
Article Text:
Repesentative image

A first-of-its-kind insurance policy

How the technology works

The 'Jesus-level technology'

Clinical trials in China and safety concerns

Government push

Elon Musk has spent years pursuing what he has called "Jesus-level" technology through Neuralink, aiming to treat chronic health conditions by implanting computer chips directly into the human brain. But that vision may end up taking shape fastest not in the US, but in China, where state authorities have launched a coordinated push to accelerate the country's own brain-computer interface (BCI) industry, according to a South China Morning Post report. China has introduced its first commercial policy covering invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) surgery. State-owned PICC Property and Casualty announced the scheme in partnership with a hospital affiliated with Zhejiang University School of Medicine in Hangzhou, a tech hub home to leading AI and robotics start-ups.Over the past few days, a string of BCI-related initiatives have been announced across China, involving state insurers, investment banks and local governments alike. The most significant came on Wednesday, when PICC Property and Casualty, a major state-owned insurer, announced it had signed the country's first commercial insurance policy covering the invasive surgery typically required to implant a BCI device in a patient's brain.The announcement moved markets almost immediately, with BCI-linked stocks in Hong Kong climbing as investors bet that insurance coverage would help speed up the technology's path to commercial use. Shares of BCI-related firms rose 1.59% on Wednesday, with neuro-interventional device maker Shanghai Heartcare Medical Technology up 1.28% and software developer BrainAurora Medical Technology gaining 1.65%.The BCI technology, which conventionally involves open-skull surgery to implant electrodes in a targeted region of the brain, allows patients to control digital devices using thought alone. The field has been most prominently championed globally by Musk's Neuralink, and versions of the technology have already been tested on human patients in both the US and China, in some cases showing promise in helping patients paralysed from the neck down regain the ability to move.The public hospital involved in PICC's new insurance scheme is regarded by local officials and doctors as a leading centre for BCI clinical trials in the region, and has reportedly conducted at least 12 human trials involving BCI implants, according to Chinese media reports. In one recent case, a 61-year-old paraplegic patient with a spinal cord injury regained the ability to bend and lift his leg within three days of surgery, and was walking unassisted by the fifteenth day.Brain-computer interfaces allow signals generated by the brain to be converted into digital commands that can control computers, devices or prosthetics. Musk has repeatedly promoted the technology's potential to transform lives. Speaking via video link at an event in Israel this week, Musk argued that his company, Neuralink, does not receive enough recognition for its achievements."Restoring control of people who are tetraplegics and restoring sight, I think, are pretty big deals," Musk said. "They're sort of what I might call Jesus-level technologies," he added. Neuralink has said its implants could eventually allow users to type, move a computer cursor and operate devices using only their thoughts. Supporters of the technology envision an even more ambitious future, where people could communicate digitally through thoughts or interact with machines without physical input.BCI technology, championed by Elon Musk’s Neuralink, requires open-skull surgery to implant electrodes that allow patients to control digital devices with their thoughts. In Hangzhou, doctors have conducted at least 12 human trials. In one case, a 61-year-old paraplegic regained the ability to walk unassisted within 15 days of surgery.Clinicians cautioned that safety must remain the top priority. “We don’t yet have long-term safety data from BCI clinical trials. There’s no data spanning several years,” said Duan Wanru, chief physician at Xuanwu Hospital in Beijing, during the Global Health Summit in Hong Kong.Alongside the insurance policy, the Zhejiang provincial government announced plans to boost financing for BCI firms and encourage them to go public. The coordinated effort underscores China’s ambition to lead in brain-computer interface technology, potentially outpacing Musk’s vision of “Jesus-level” implants to treat chronic conditions.
Article Summary: China has introduced its first commercial policy covering invasive brain-computer interface (bci) surgery. State-owned picc property and casualty announced the scheme in partnership with a hospital affiliated with zhejiang university school of medicine in hangzhou. In hangzhou, doctors have conducted at least 12 human trials.

Article Title: America’s biggest investor Michael Burry, who warned Wall Street of 2008 housing crisis, is not happy with Oracle and Micron, here's why
Article Text:
Michael Burry’s concerns about Oracle

The AI hype problem of Micron

Michael Burry is not happy with reports of Nvidia investing $250 billion in OpenAI

America’s biggest investor Michael Burry who famous for warning about the 2008 housing crisis has taken aim at two major technology players Oracle and Micron Technology. According to a report by The Street, known for his contrarian bets, Burry argues that both companies are overexposed to the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom and weighed down by financial commitments that could backfire if demand slows.As per the report, Burry disclosed a short position against Oracle, highlighting its massive spending on AI infrastructure. The company has signed long-term leases and GPU capacity contracts worth hundreds of billions, far exceeding its current revenue base. Despite the strong operating cash flow, Oracle reported negative free cash flow due to surging capital expenditures. Burry warns that if AI demand falters, Oracle could be left with costly obligations and declining returns.Micron Technology is also in Burry’s crosshairs. He expanded his short bet against the chipmaker, arguing its recent rally is driven more by investor enthusiasm for AI than by solid fundamentals. Micron has historically struggled with cyclical downturns, and Burry believes its profitability remains vulnerable despite the current boom.Burry’s bearish stance extends beyond individual companies. He has also shorted the iShares Semiconductor ETF and Nebius Group, signaling broader doubts about the sustainability of AI-linked stocks.His thesis centers on off-balance-sheet liabilities: companies committing billions to long-term infrastructure at inflated prices, which could become burdensome if growth slows.Recently, Michael Burry voiced his sharp criticism of reports that Nvidia is preparing a a $250 billion backstop for OpenAI’s massive Ohio data-center project. According to a report by the Wall Street journal, the guarantees would help OpenAI lease a 10-gigawatt site being developed by SoftBank’s SB Energy, with total costs potentially exceeding $500 billion. Burry’s complaint echoes what analysts have long warned about in AI megadeals: circular funding arrangements that expose investors to enormous risk if sentiment shifts or growth slows. Nvidia, already valued at $5 trillion, has invested $30 billion in OpenAI and is now considering financing chip purchases worth another $350 billion. Critics say such structures could leave the industry vulnerable, especially since OpenAI remains unprofitable and lacks an investment-grade credit rating.Michael Burry’s criticism underscores growing unease about the sustainability of $100 billion-plus AI financing structures. His warning suggests that while AI demand is surging, the industry’s reliance on complex guarantees and debt-backed megaprojects could become its biggest vulnerability.
Article Summary: America’s biggest investor michael burry has taken aim at two major technology players oracle and micron technology. Burry argues that both companies are overexposed to the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom and weighed down by financial commitments that could backfire if demand slows.

Article Title: Oracle layoffs: As Oracle leadership prepares to send ‘6am layoff email’ on September 1, company asks managers to give a list of…
Article Text:
Oracle cut 21,000 jobs last year. Another round is coming this month

Oracle layoffs in March arrived as 6AM emails for 10,000+ employees and ended the same working day

Oracle has burned through almost all of its $2.1 billion restructuring budget

Why Oracle's $55.7 billion AI data centre spending keeps the pressure on headcount

Oracle is lining up another round of job cuts this month, and the deadline is set by its own calendar. Managers have been asked to draw up lists of employees whose roles are being eliminated, with the company looking to bring payroll down before September 1—the day its fiscal second quarter opens. Business Insider, which first reported the plan citing people familiar with it and an internal document, said reductions on some teams could reach double-digit percentages.The cuts would land on top of a year in which the company already removed about 21,000 full-time roles, roughly 13% of its workforce. Headcount fell from around 162,000 in May 2025 to about 141,000 at the end of May 2026, with roughly 49,000 of those remaining in the United States. What makes this round sting is Oracle's own explanation. Its annual filing attributes part of the decline to the company's adoption and deployment of AI—the same technology it is borrowing tens of billions of dollars to sell.Employees cut on March 31 found out first thing in the morning. The notification, sent from "Oracle Leadership," told recipients their role had been eliminated as part of a broader organisational change and that it was their last working day.Staff in both the US and India were affected. LinkedIn posts from those let go pointed to Oracle Health, Sales, Cloud, Customer Success and NetSuite. Roughly 10,000 positions went in that single wave.The email itself was brisk. It thanked employees for their contributions, told them severance paperwork would arrive via DocuSign, and asked them to submit a personal email address immediately—because access to their computer, email and files was about to be switched off.Severance is not cheap. Oracle booked $1.8 billion in restructuring costs in FY2026, up from $374 million a year earlier, a 391% jump. Its 10-K, filed on June 22, capped the total expected cost of the plan at $2.1 billion, which leaves only about $300 million of headroom. Cuts at the scale Business Insider describes would either have to fit inside that remainder or push Oracle into its second new restructuring plan in three years. TD Cowen analysts estimated in January that shedding 20,000 to 30,000 workers could unlock $8 billion to $10 billion.The money is going somewhere specific. Capital expenditure hit $55.7 billion in FY2026, up from $21.2 billion the year before, as Oracle raced to build data centres for customers including OpenAI. It raised $43 billion in debt and $5 billion in equity over the year, expects around $40 billion more in FY2027, and ran free cash flow of negative $23.7 billion. Interest expense alone climbed to $4.6 billion from $3.6 billion.The underlying business is not the problem. FY2026 revenue rose 17% to $67.4 billion, cloud infrastructure revenue grew 77%, and remaining performance obligations closed the year at $638 billion after ending Q3 at $553 billion. Oracle has also told investors that AI code generation is letting it reorganise product development into smaller teams, saying the technology helps it build "more software in less time with fewer people. "That sentence, written for shareholders in March, reads differently in August. Investors have not been won over either—the stock is down more than 20% this year, and shareholders sued in January over what Oracle said about how much it would need to borrow to service its $300 billion OpenAI commitment.For the employees on this month's lists, the reasoning is beside the point. The jobs are being removed to meet a date on a fiscal calendar, and the payoff Oracle is betting on will arrive after they have gone.
Article Summary: Oracle has burned through almost all of its $2.1 billion restructuring budget. The company cut 21,000 full-time roles last year, roughly 13% of its workforce. It attributes part of the decline to the company's adoption and deployment of ai.

Article Title: Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings on why he stopped calling CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters about the business: They can mimic me and...
Article Text:
Reed Hastings on leaving the Netflix board: 'like being a godparent versus a parent'

The Warner Bros. Discovery call Netflix made without its founder in the room

Netflix's co-founder Reed Hastings spent 29 years at Netflix and now sends its two CEOs almost nothing. Not because anything soured — the opposite. He says Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters have absorbed his thinking so completely that phoning them is redundant. He's tested that theory in the biggest way possible. When Netflix walked away from the Warner Bros. Discovery deal this year, its founder wasn't in the room for the call.Speaking on Semafor's The CEO Signal podcast, hosted by Penny Pritzker and Andrew Edgecliffe-Johnson, the Netflix co-founder said he's been "very disciplined" about not calling the co-CEOs on business matters since leaving the board in June. He tried, briefly. For the first couple of months he lobbed in the occasional thought, then noticed something: they could already run the simulation without him. They ask what Reed would think, set that answer aside, and do what they believe is right. Which, Hastings said, is what they should do. "They can mimic me and conjure me easily. I'm very predictable in that way."The social side hasn't gone anywhere—he still talks to them and they hang out.What changed was the front line. Hastings stepped down as Netflix CEO in January 2023 and left the board this June, and he's blunt that the second exit was the smaller one. Being on a board of a company doing well, he said, is a fairly relaxed gig. The genuinely disorienting part was the workload dropping from around 70 hours a week to roughly one.The clearest proof of the handover came this year, when Netflix walked away from the Warner Bros. Discovery deal. Hastings says he wasn't involved in that decision at all. Sarandos and Peters worked the trade-offs themselves. He describes it as a price question rather than a strategy one—Netflix was comfortable with what it had offered, Larry Ellison raised the bid, Netflix had the chance to match and chose not to.Hastings frames the whole shift as moving from parent to godparent. The company, he added, has to stop reliving how he did things and start making its own mistakes.
Article Summary: Reed hastings spent 29 years at netflix and now sends its two ceos almost nothing. He says ted sarandos and greg peters have absorbed his thinking so completely that phoning them is redundant. When netflix walked away from the warner bros. Discovery deal this year, its founder wasn't in the room for the call.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies





AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.
